events.title: Laravel 8.0 released
events.summary: Taylor Otwell released Laravel 8.0 on September 8, 2020 with model factories, job batching, and improved routing and maintenance mode.
events.about: Laravel 8 refined the developer experience before Laravel 9's PHP 8 jump: class-based model factories replaced legacy definitions; job batching coordinated queues; Jetstream offered optional auth scaffolding. It remained the default PHP framework for [SaaS] and agency work through the early 2020s.

narrative.whyChosen: Laravel 8 polished factories and queues for production PHP teams.
narrative.whyImportant: Job batching and modern factories reduced boilerplate in data-heavy apps.
narrative.problemSolved: Legacy factory syntax and ad-hoc queue orchestration slowed Laravel testing and ops.

events.title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 2 released
events.summary: Samsung began selling the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 2 — refined hinge and larger cover display — foldables became more durable.
events.about: Foldables forced Android developers to handle resizable and multi-window layouts on flexible displays. Refined hinge and larger cover display — foldables became more durable.

narrative.whyChosen: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 2 pushed foldable Android hardware into the mainstream.
narrative.whyImportant: Foldable form factors require adaptive [UI] patterns beyond fixed phone screens.
narrative.problemSolved: Phones were locked to a single rigid screen size and aspect ratio.

events.title: Vue 3.0 released
events.summary: Evan You shipped Vue 3.0 on September 18, 2020 with the Composition [API], a faster virtual DOM, and better TypeScript support.
events.about: Vue 3 let teams organize component logic with composables instead of sprawling `data`/`methods` blocks — similar ergonomics to React hooks with Vue's reactive system. The rewrite improved performance for large dashboards and became the default for new Laravel, Nuxt, and enterprise frontends.

narrative.whyChosen: Vue 3 was a ground-up rewrite that kept Vue's gentle learning curve while scaling to large apps.
narrative.whyImportant: The Composition [API] and improved TypeScript story kept Vue competitive with React for new projects.
narrative.problemSolved: Vue 2's options [API] did not scale cleanly for complex components shared across big codebases.
